issues.sym: The car hesitates or barely responds to the gas pedal, surges or lunges forward unexpectedly, gets stuck at low speed, or stalls while driving.
issues.why: Owners and shops point to the electronic throttle system: the throttle body or its motor, the accelerator pedal position switch, or the engine computer. Some cars needed a computer reflash; others went through several throttle bodies.
issues.next: If the car surges or stalls, pull over safely and have it towed rather than driven. Ask the shop to read throttle and pedal sensor codes and check for engine computer updates before replacing parts.

issues.t: Brake lights may fail, shifter stuck in Park (recall)
issues.sym: Brake lights that do not light (or stay on), cruise control that does not cancel when you brake, a stability control light, or a shifter that will not leave Park.
issues.why: The brake pedal (stop lamp) switch can work only intermittently. Kia recalled 2006-2007 Amantis (09V130) and 2007-2009 Amantis (13V114) to replace the switch.
issues.next: Have someone check your brake lights, then give your VIN to a Kia dealer to confirm the recall was done. The switch replacement is free.

issues.sym: The engine cranks but will not start, or starts only after several tries, sometimes with a flashing security light.
issues.why: A faulty immobilizer (anti-theft) control module may fail to recognize the key and block the engine from starting.
issues.next: Try your spare key. If that does not help, have a shop or dealer read immobilizer codes; the module or key may need replacing and programming.

issues.t: Headlight and tail bulbs keep burning out
issues.sym: Headlight bulbs fail again and again, or brake and tail bulbs burn out often.
issues.why: Owners report repeated headlight bulb failures, and Kia issued a bulletin for longer-life rear combination bulbs on its models.
issues.next: Replace burned-out bulbs promptly. If bulbs keep failing, have the connectors and charging voltage checked, and ask for the improved rear bulbs.

issues.t: Timing belt due on the 3.5L V6
issues.sym: Usually no warning. If the belt breaks or jumps, the engine stops suddenly and may not restart, and internal damage is possible.
issues.why: The 3.5L V6 uses a rubber timing belt that must be replaced on schedule (typically 60,000 to 90,000 miles). These cars are well past their first interval.
issues.next: If there is no record of a belt change, have the belt, tensioner and idler pulleys replaced soon. Many owners also replace the water pump at the same time.

issues.sym: Shifts are harsh or delayed, the engine revs without the car speeding up, or the car struggles to shift.
issues.why: Internal wear in the 5-speed automatic causes slipping. Kia also issued a procedure to reset and relearn the transmission adaptive shift values.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition. Ask a shop to try the adaptive relearn first; if slipping continues, a rebuild or replacement may be needed.

issues.sym: A rattle or chatter from the engine for a few seconds after starting.
issues.why: Kia issued a bulletin on Lambda 3.8L engine noises. One owner had the timing chain tensioners replaced and was later told the noise was normal.
issues.next: Note how long the noise lasts. A brief rattle that fades may be normal; a noise that stays or gets louder should be checked, and keep up oil changes with the right oil.

issues.t: Oil leak at the back of the engine misdiagnosed
issues.sym: Oil dripping at the rear of the engine or transmission joint, often blamed on the rear main seal or oil pan.
issues.why: On the 3.8L, oil can run down from drain holes in the engine valley, the oil filter housing, the oil pressure switch or a gasket. Kia warned technicians that this is often mistaken for a rear main seal leak.
issues.next: Before paying for a rear main seal job, ask the shop to check the valley, oil filter housing and oil pressure switch as Kia bulletin PS-211 describes.

issues.t: Rough idle or cam timing codes
issues.sym: Rough idle, poor acceleration, misfires, or a check engine light with cam timing codes.
issues.why: The oil control valve in the variable valve timing system can stick or fail. Kia issued a bulletin on checking it for these symptoms.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Change the oil on time, since dirty oil can make these valves stick.

issues.t: Check engine light fixed by computer update
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on but the car drives normally, with codes such as P0110 or other powertrain codes.
issues.why: Kia released engine computer software upgrades for some 3.8L engines that set false or nuisance codes.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask a Kia dealer whether a software update applies before replacing parts.

issues.t: Check engine light from oxygen sensor codes
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with oxygen sensor (HO2S) codes, sometimes with worse fuel economy.
issues.why: Kia issued a bulletin for oxygen sensor codes on the Amanti, Sedona and Sorento.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask about the bulletin. A failed sensor should be replaced to pass emissions.

issues.t: Check engine light from evaporative system codes
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with EVAP codes such as P0446 or P2422.
issues.why: The evaporative system canister vent or close valve, which controls fuel vapors from the tank, can fail or clog. Kia issued bulletins on diagnosing these codes and inspecting the valve.
issues.next: Check the gas cap first. If the light returns, have the EVAP canister close valve inspected under the Kia bulletins.

issues.sym: The battery goes dead after the car sits, even when fairly new.
issues.why: Something stays powered after the car is shut off, or the battery itself is weak.
issues.next: Have the battery and charging system tested and a parasitic draw test done to find what stays on.
